integrity: The complete sixteen-page Lorenz–Emanuel source was inspected at the exact model equation, cyclic indexing, energy-conserving advection statement, global moment balance, variance parabola, linear stability calculation, and chaotic F=8 discussion. Its full searchable text contains no conditional or covariance formulation. The open Kerin–Engler article record was inspected through its model/generalization scope, bifurcation figures, energy discussion, references, and subject classification; targeted searches found no conditional, variance, or stationary-measure formulation. The Gallavotti–Lucarini public preprint record was checked for its energy-conserving advection and nonequilibrium-ensemble scope. A recent conditional-mean Lorenz–96 preprint was compared at abstract level and addresses Fourier coarse-to-fine recoverability rather than local advective transfer. The sitewise generator proof, conditional residual identity, site-time covariance decomposition, and equilibrium equality case were independently reconstructed and replayed with the packaged exact checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the standard one-scale Lorenz–96 equation, not stochastic, two-scale, or site-dependent variants.
It determines the local conditional mean and residual variance of nonlinear advection, not the full conditional distribution.
The global site-time variance parabola is classical prior work and is used only as an input to the new activity decomposition.
The original 1996 introduction was not available with a checked day-resolved public date; the structured date uses the earliest checked day-resolved full public same-model source.
The 2014 nonequilibrium-ensemble source was not available as a completely parsed local copy in the checked route.
An equivalent short one-site generator identity could remain in unindexed literature.
title: Exact local advection regression and activity decomposition in Lorenz–96
